text:
Ravi Desai: hey team — about to open my first PR. what's the quick-to-follow checklist for branch names, commit headers, and reviewers? also curious which CI gates are must-pass before we merge.

Marta Lopez: welcome Ravi! shortest checklist: 1) branch from main, name like `team-ticket-short` (e.g., runtime-789-kv-cache). 2) commit header: `pkg: brief summary` (<=50 chars). 3) run pre-commit and unit tests locally. 4) add a short PR description + test plan.

Eli Ford: reviewers: CODEOWNERS auto-adds primary reviewers — but please explicitly add one peer reviewer from your squad for context. For platform/runtime touching code ping @eng-runtime and for infra ping @eng-infra.

Ravi Desai: do we require any signoffs or a DCO?

Marta Lopez: yes, signoff/DCO is required. use `git commit -s` or add `Signed-off-by:` in commit body. CI will check it.

merge-bot: CI summary you'll see: pre-commit hooks, ruff/black, pytest unit, mypy/type checks, license check, and if you touched `serving/` or `infra/` an extended smoke job runs on the dedicated pipeline. Failure posts a failed check on the PR.

Eli Ford: merge policy: default is squash-and-merge for single logical changes. If you're landing a multi-commit refactor keep separate commits and add a note in the PR explaining history. For release branches we sometimes allow a merge commit to preserve bump history.

Ravi Desai: any quick local commands to avoid running the whole CI? some checks are slow.

Marta Lopez: run `pre-commit run --all-files`, `pytest tests/unit -q` and `poetry run mypy pkg/yourpkg`. We have `make fast-checks` which runs the fast gate locally. For cross-package changes use `scripts/affected-tests.sh` to run only impacted tests.

Eli Ford: add a brief `changes:` section in the PR body for any user-visible behavior changes, and attach screenshots or logs for API changes. If you need an expedited review add the `prio/high` label and explain why.

Ravi Desai: thanks — one more: code owners auto-request — can I add additional reviewers?

Marta Lopez: absolutely. add them in the reviewers box or `@mention` in the PR thread. Also check CONTRIBUTING.md for commit examples.

onboard-bot: Tip: newcomers  post a link to your PR in #new-hires for extra eyeballs and follow the PR checklist: https://redwood.example/docs/pr-checklist :robot_face:

Ravi Desai: great, I'll push up `runtime-789-kv-cache` and ping reviewers once CI is clean. appreciate the help! :thumbsup:
